-- Cfx.re Lua runtime (client and server): the global `msgpack` library. The
-- runtime uses citizenfx/lua-cmsgpack, an API-compatible C replacement of
-- lua-MessagePack.

---
--- MessagePack serializer used by the runtime for event arguments, exports
--- and state bags. Available as the global `msgpack` and through
--- `require 'msgpack'`.
---
--- The runtime configures it with `set_string('string_compat')`,
--- `set_integer('unsigned')`, `set_array('without_hole')` and the
--- `empty_table_as_array` option. Vectors, quaternions, function references
--- and the `Entity` / `Player` wrappers have dedicated extension types.
---
--- [Documentation](https://docs.fivem.net/docs/scripting-manual/runtimes/lua/#external-libraries)
---@class msgpack
---@field null function @Sentinel representing an explicit `nil` (alias: `sentinel`).
---@field sentinel function @Sentinel representing an explicit `nil` (alias: `null`).
---@field packers table @Generic packer functions, indexed by type name.
---@field _NAME string @Library name.
---@field _VERSION string @Library version.
---@field _COPYRIGHT string @Copyright notice.
---@field _DESCRIPTION string @Library description.
msgpack = {}

---
--- A persistent packing buffer created by `msgpack.new()`.
---
--- * `packer(...)` (also `packer + value` and `packer << value`) encodes and
---   appends values.
--- * `packer .. encoded` appends already encoded data.
--- * `tostring(packer)` returns the encoded string and `#packer` its length.
---
--- The methods below encode their arguments with an explicit MessagePack type
--- and return the packer, so calls can be chained. The `nil`, `true` and
--- `false` methods, whose names are Lua keywords, are declared under their
--- aliases `null`, `t` and `f`.
---@class MsgpackPacker
local MsgpackPackerType = {}

---
--- Appends the values with automatic type detection (like `packer(...)`).
---@vararg any
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:any(...) end

---
--- Appends a MessagePack `nil`.
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:null() end

---
--- Appends a MessagePack `true`.
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:t() end

---
--- Appends a MessagePack `false`.
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:f() end

---
--- Appends the values encoded as booleans.
---@vararg any
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:boolean(...) end

---
--- Appends the values encoded as strings, following the configured string
--- option.
---@vararg string
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:string(...) end

---
--- Appends the values encoded as MessagePack v5 strings, ignoring the
--- configured string option.
---@vararg string
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:_string(...) end

---
--- Appends the values encoded as MessagePack v4 (raw) strings.
---@vararg string
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:string_compat(...) end

---
--- Appends the values encoded as binary data.
---@vararg string
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:binary(...) end

---
--- Appends the tables encoded as MessagePack maps.
---@vararg table
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:map(...) end

---
--- Appends the tables encoded as MessagePack arrays.
---@vararg table
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:array(...) end

---
--- Appends the tables encoded as arrays or maps depending on their content,
--- using the registered extensions.
---@vararg table
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:table(...) end

---
--- Appends the tables encoded as arrays or maps depending on their content,
--- ignoring the registered extensions.
---@vararg table
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:_table(...) end

---
--- Appends the values encoded as integers.
---@vararg number
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:integer(...) end

---
--- Appends the values encoded as signed integers.
---@vararg number
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:signed(...) end

---
--- Appends the values encoded as unsigned integers.
---@vararg number
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:unsigned(...) end

---
--- Appends the values encoded as 32-bit floats.
---@vararg number
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:float(...) end

---
--- Appends the values encoded as 64-bit floats.
---@vararg number
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:double(...) end

---
--- Appends the values encoded as numbers (integer or float, following the
--- configured number option).
---@vararg number
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:number(...) end

---
--- Appends the values encoded as unsigned 8-bit integers, in the smallest
--- MessagePack format that holds them.
---@vararg number
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:uint8(...) end

---
--- Appends the values encoded as unsigned 16-bit integers, in the smallest
--- MessagePack format that holds them.
---@vararg number
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:uint16(...) end

---
--- Appends the values encoded as unsigned 32-bit integers, in the smallest
--- MessagePack format that holds them.
---@vararg number
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:uint32(...) end

---
--- Appends the values encoded as unsigned 64-bit integers, in the smallest
--- MessagePack format that holds them.
---@vararg number
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:uint64(...) end

---
--- Appends the values encoded as signed 8-bit integers, in the smallest
--- MessagePack format that holds them.
---@vararg number
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:int8(...) end

---
--- Appends the values encoded as signed 16-bit integers, in the smallest
--- MessagePack format that holds them.
---@vararg number
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:int16(...) end

---
--- Appends the values encoded as signed 32-bit integers, in the smallest
--- MessagePack format that holds them.
---@vararg number
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:int32(...) end

---
--- Appends the values encoded as signed 64-bit integers, in the smallest
--- MessagePack format that holds them.
---@vararg number
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:int64(...) end

---
--- Appends the values encoded as unsigned 8-bit integers, always in the
--- fixed-size `uint8` format.
---@vararg number
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:fix_uint8(...) end

---
--- Appends the values encoded as unsigned 16-bit integers, always in the
--- fixed-size `uint16` format.
---@vararg number
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:fix_uint16(...) end

---
--- Appends the values encoded as unsigned 32-bit integers, always in the
--- fixed-size `uint32` format.
---@vararg number
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:fix_uint32(...) end

---
--- Appends the values encoded as unsigned 64-bit integers, always in the
--- fixed-size `uint64` format.
---@vararg number
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:fix_uint64(...) end

---
--- Appends the values encoded as signed 8-bit integers, always in the
--- fixed-size `int8` format.
---@vararg number
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:fix_int8(...) end

---
--- Appends the values encoded as signed 16-bit integers, always in the
--- fixed-size `int16` format.
---@vararg number
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:fix_int16(...) end

---
--- Appends the values encoded as signed 32-bit integers, always in the
--- fixed-size `int32` format.
---@vararg number
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:fix_int32(...) end

---
--- Appends the values encoded as signed 64-bit integers, always in the
--- fixed-size `int64` format.
---@vararg number
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:fix_int64(...) end

---
--- Appends the values encoded as C `char` integers.
---@vararg number
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:char(...) end

---
--- Appends the values encoded as C `signed char` integers.
---@vararg number
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:signed_char(...) end

---
--- Appends the values encoded as C `unsigned char` integers.
---@vararg number
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:unsigned_char(...) end

---
--- Appends the values encoded as C `short` integers.
---@vararg number
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:short(...) end

---
--- Appends the values encoded as C `long` integers.
---@vararg number
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:long(...) end

---
--- Appends the values encoded as C `long long` integers.
---@vararg number
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:long_long(...) end

---
--- Appends the values encoded as C `unsigned short` integers.
---@vararg number
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:unsigned_short(...) end

---
--- Appends the values encoded as C `unsigned int` integers.
---@vararg number
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:unsigned_int(...) end

---
--- Appends the values encoded as C `unsigned long` integers.
---@vararg number
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:unsigned_long(...) end

---
--- Appends the values encoded as C `unsigned long long` integers.
---@vararg number
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:unsigned_long_long(...) end

---
--- Appends the values encoded as signed 16-bit integers.
---@vararg number
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:signed_int16(...) end

---
--- Appends the values encoded as signed 32-bit integers.
---@vararg number
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:signed_int32(...) end

---
--- Appends the values encoded as signed 64-bit integers.
---@vararg number
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:signed_int64(...) end

---
--- Appends the vectors and quaternions encoded with their MessagePack extension
--- types.
---@vararg vector2|vector3|vector4|quat
---@return MsgpackPacker @This packer.
function MsgpackPackerType:vector(...) end

---
--- Serializes the arguments and returns the concatenated MessagePack data.
---
--- ```lua
--- local data = msgpack.pack({ 1, 2, 3 }, 'text')
--- ```
---@vararg any
---@return string @The encoded data.
function msgpack.pack(...) end

---
--- Serializes the arguments as one MessagePack array, so that
--- `table.unpack(msgpack.unpack(data))` restores them, including `nil`
--- arguments. This is the format of event payloads.
---@vararg any
---@return string @The encoded array.
function msgpack.pack_args(...) end

---
--- Deserializes MessagePack data and returns every decoded value.
---
--- ```lua
--- local t, s = msgpack.unpack(msgpack.pack({ 1, 2 }, 'x'))
--- ```
---@overload fun(data:string):any
---@param data string @The encoded data.
---@param offset integer @Position to start decoding at (default 1).
---@param limit integer @Maximum number of values to decode (default: all).
---@param endPosition integer @Position to stop decoding at.
---@return any @The decoded values.
function msgpack.unpack(data, offset, limit, endPosition) end

---
--- Decodes values one at a time. Returns the position of the next value
--- (`0` when the end of the data is reached) followed by the decoded values.
---
--- ```lua
--- local position, value = 1, nil
--- while position ~= 0 do
---     position, value = msgpack.next(data, position, 1)
--- end
--- ```
---@overload fun(data:string):integer, any
---@param data string @The encoded data.
---@param position integer @Position to start decoding at (default 1).
---@param limit integer @Maximum number of values to decode.
---@param endPosition integer @Position to stop decoding at.
---@return integer, any @The next position (0 at the end), then the decoded values.
function msgpack.next(data, position, limit, endPosition) end

---
--- Creates a persistent packer that accumulates encoded values.
---
--- ```lua
--- local packer = msgpack.new()
--- packer(1, 2, math.pi)
--- packer:float(4.0)
--- local data = tostring(packer)
--- ```
---@return MsgpackPacker @The new packer.
function msgpack.new() end

---
--- Sets a global packing/unpacking option. Number options: `'float'`,
--- `'double'`, `'integer'`, `'unsigned'`; string options: `'string_compat'`,
--- `'string_binary'`; table options: `'always_as_map'`, `'without_hole'`,
--- `'with_hole'`, `'empty_table_as_array'`, `'sentinel'`; type option:
--- `'ignore_invalid'`; lua-MessagePack compatibility options: `'small_lua'`,
--- `'full64bits'`, `'long_double'`.
---@param option string|'"float"'|'"double"'|'"integer"'|'"unsigned"'|'"string_compat"'|'"string_binary"'|'"always_as_map"'|'"without_hole"'|'"with_hole"'|'"empty_table_as_array"'|'"sentinel"'|'"ignore_invalid"'|'"small_lua"'|'"full64bits"'|'"long_double"' @The option name.
---@param value boolean @Whether the option is enabled.
function msgpack.setoption(option, value) end

---
--- Returns the value of a global packing/unpacking option.
---@param option string @The option name (see `msgpack.setoption`).
---@return any @The option value.
function msgpack.getoption(option) end

---
--- Returns `true` when the library was built in "safe" mode (every function
--- wrapped in a protected call).
---@return boolean @Whether safe mode is enabled.
function msgpack.safe() end

---
--- lua-MessagePack compatibility: selects how strings are encoded.
---@param mode string|'"string"'|'"string_compat"'|'"string_binary"' @The string encoding.
function msgpack.set_string(mode) end

---
--- lua-MessagePack compatibility: selects how array-like tables are encoded.
---@param mode string|'"without_hole"'|'"with_hole"'|'"always_as_map"' @The table encoding.
function msgpack.set_array(mode) end

---
--- lua-MessagePack compatibility: selects how integers are encoded.
---@param mode string|'"signed"'|'"unsigned"' @The integer encoding.
function msgpack.set_integer(mode) end

---
--- lua-MessagePack compatibility: selects how floats are encoded.
---@param mode string|'"float"'|'"double"' @The float encoding.
function msgpack.set_number(mode) end

---
--- Registers an extension type. `encoder` is usually a metatable providing
--- `__ext` (the extension id, 0-127), `__pack(self, extId)` returning the
--- encoded payload and `__unpack(payload, extId)` returning the decoded value.
---
--- The Cfx runtime reserves the ids 10 and 11 (function references), 41
--- (`Entity`) and 42 (`Player`).
---@param encoder table @The extension definition.
---@return table @The extension definition.
function msgpack.extend(encoder) end

---
--- Returns the extension definition registered for `extId`.
---@param extId integer @The extension id.
---@return table|nil @The extension definition, or `nil`.
function msgpack.extend_get(extId) end

---
--- Removes the extension definitions of every id given as argument.
---@vararg integer
function msgpack.extend_clear(...) end

---
--- Associates a Lua type name (as returned by `type`) with an extension, so
--- values of that type are packed with it.
---@overload fun(typeName:string)
---@param typeName string @The Lua type name, for example `'function'`.
---@param extension integer|table @An extension id or an extension definition.
function msgpack.settype(typeName, extension) end

---
--- Returns the extension associated with a Lua type name.
---@param typeName string @The Lua type name.
---@return any @The associated extension, or `nil`.
function msgpack.gettype(typeName) end

-- Cfx.re Lua runtime (client and server): the global `promise` library
-- (zserge/lua-promises, loaded from `deferred.lua`). The library and the
-- promises it creates are described by two classes: `PromiseLib` (the type of
-- the global `promise`) and `promise` (the promise instances).

---
--- A promise created by `promise.new()`. Settle it with `resolve` or `reject`,
--- chain callbacks with `next`, and wait for it inside a scheduler thread with
--- `Citizen.Await`.
---
--- [Documentation](https://docs.fivem.net/docs/scripting-reference/runtimes/lua/functions/promise.new/)
---@class promise
---@field state integer @0 pending, 1 resolving, 2 rejecting, 3 resolved, 4 rejected.
---@field value any @The resolved value or the rejection reason, once settled.
local PromiseType = {}

---
--- Resolves the promise with `value`. Has no effect if the promise is already
--- settled.
---@param value any @The resolved value.
---@return promise @This promise.
function PromiseType:resolve(value) end

---
--- Rejects the promise with `reason`. Has no effect if the promise is already
--- settled.
---@param reason any @The rejection reason.
---@return promise @This promise.
function PromiseType:reject(reason) end

---
--- Registers callbacks called when the promise settles and returns a new
--- promise for the value they return. Either callback can be `nil`.
---
--- ```lua
--- p:next(function(value)
---     print('resolved', value)
--- end, function(reason)
---     print('rejected', reason)
--- end)
--- ```
---@overload fun(onResolve:fun(value:any):any):promise
---@param onResolve fun(value:any):any @Called with the resolved value.
---@param onReject fun(reason:any):any @Called with the rejection reason.
---@return promise @A promise of the callback result.
function PromiseType:next(onResolve, onReject) end

---
--- The global promise library: `promise.new`, `promise.all`, `promise.map` and
--- `promise.first` create promises (see the `promise` class for their
--- methods).
---
--- ```lua
--- local p = promise.new()
--- SetTimeout(500, function()
---     p:resolve(42)
--- end)
--- local value = Citizen.Await(p)
--- ```
---
--- [Documentation](https://docs.fivem.net/docs/scripting-reference/runtimes/lua/functions/promise.new/)
---@class PromiseLib
local PromiseLibType = {}

---
--- Creates a new pending promise.
---
--- If `options` is a function, it is called with the new promise; an error
--- raised by it rejects the promise. A table can provide `success` and
--- `failure` callbacks and an `extend` function called with the new promise.
---
--- [Documentation](https://docs.fivem.net/docs/scripting-reference/runtimes/lua/functions/promise.new/)
---@overload fun():promise
---@param options fun(p:promise)|table @Initializer function, or a `{ success, failure, extend }` table.
---@return promise @The new promise.
function PromiseLibType.new(options) end

---
--- Returns a promise that settles once every promise of `promises` has
--- settled. It resolves with the array of results, or rejects with that array
--- if any of the promises was rejected. An empty list resolves immediately.
---
--- [Documentation](https://docs.fivem.net/docs/scripting-reference/runtimes/lua/functions/promise.all/)
---@param promises promise[] @The promises to wait for.
---@return promise @A promise of the array of results.
function PromiseLibType.all(promises) end

---
--- Calls `mapper` on each element of `values` one after the other, waiting for
--- the promise it returns before moving on. The returned promise resolves with
--- the array of results, or rejects with the first rejection reason.
---
--- [Documentation](https://docs.fivem.net/docs/scripting-reference/runtimes/lua/functions/promise.map/)
---@param values any[] @The values to map.
---@param mapper fun(value:any):promise @Function returning a promise for each value.
---@return promise @A promise of the array of results.
function PromiseLibType.map(values, mapper) end

---
--- Returns a promise that settles like the first promise of `promises` to
--- settle.
---
--- [Documentation](https://docs.fivem.net/docs/scripting-reference/runtimes/lua/functions/promise.first/)
---@param promises promise[] @The competing promises.
---@return promise @A promise settled by the first one to settle.
function PromiseLibType.first(promises) end

---
--- The global promise library (see `PromiseLib`): `promise.new()` creates a
--- promise, `promise.all`, `promise.map` and `promise.first` combine
--- promises.
---
--- [Documentation](https://docs.fivem.net/docs/scripting-reference/runtimes/lua/functions/promise.new/)
---@type PromiseLib
promise = nil

local lastSent

local function postal()
  local res = Config.postalResource
  if not res or GetResourceState(res) ~= 'started' then return nil end
  local ok, value = pcall(function() return exports[res]:getPostal() end)
  if ok and (type(value) == 'string' or type(value) == 'number') then return tostring(value) end
  return nil
end

local function labels()
  local c = GetEntityCoords(PlayerPedId())
  local streetHash, crossHash = GetStreetNameAtCoord(c.x, c.y, c.z)
  local street = GetStreetNameFromHashKey(streetHash)
  local cross = crossHash ~= 0 and GetStreetNameFromHashKey(crossHash) or nil
  return street, cross, postal(), GetNameOfZone(c.x, c.y, c.z)
end

local labelsRunning = false

local function onDuty()
  return LocalPlayer.state['statewide:unit'] ~= nil
end

local function sendLabels()
  local street, cross, code, zone = labels()
  local key = ('%s|%s|%s|%s'):format(street or '', cross or '', code or '', zone or '')
  if key == lastSent then return end
  lastSent = key
  TriggerServerEvent('statewide:labels', street, cross, code, zone)
end

local function watchLabels()
  if labelsRunning then return end
  labelsRunning = true
  CreateThread(function()
    repeat
      Wait(Config.labels.minSeconds * 1000)
      if onDuty() then sendLabels() end
    until not onDuty()
    labelsRunning = false
    lastSent = nil
  end)
end

AddStateBagChangeHandler('statewide:unit', nil, function(bagName, _, value)
  if value ~= nil and bagName == ('player:%d'):format(GetPlayerServerId(PlayerId())) then watchLabels() end
end)

RegisterNetEvent('statewide:client:labelsAt', function(token, x, y, z)
  if type(token) ~= 'number' or not Pure.validCoords({ x = x, y = y, z = z }) then return end
  local streetHash, crossHash = GetStreetNameAtCoord(x + 0.0, y + 0.0, (z or 0.0) + 0.0)
  local street = GetStreetNameFromHashKey(streetHash)
  local cross = crossHash ~= 0 and GetStreetNameFromHashKey(crossHash) or nil
  TriggerServerEvent('statewide:labelsAt', token, street, cross, GetNameOfZone(x + 0.0, y + 0.0, (z or 0.0) + 0.0))
end)

RegisterNetEvent('statewide:client:labels', function()
  local street, cross, code, zone = labels()
  lastSent = ('%s|%s|%s|%s'):format(street or '', cross or '', code or '', zone or '')
  TriggerServerEvent('statewide:labels', street, cross, code, zone)
end)

CreateThread(function()
  Wait(1000)
  if onDuty() then watchLabels() end
end)

CreateThread(function()
  Wait(1000)
  local resolved = Pure.resolveCommands(Config.commands)
  if not resolved then return end
  for _, c in ipairs(resolved) do
    local params = {}
    for p in (Locale['cmd_' .. c.action .. '_params'] or ''):gmatch('%S+') do params[#params + 1] = { name = p, help = p } end
    for _, name in ipairs(c.names) do
      TriggerEvent('chat:addSuggestion', '/' .. name, Locale['cmd_' .. c.action] or '', params)
    end
  end
end)

local function callBlip(p)
  local blip = AddBlipForCoord(p.coords.x, p.coords.y, p.coords.z or 0.0)
  SetBlipSprite(blip, 280)
  SetBlipColour(blip, 1)
  SetBlipScale(blip, 1.0)
  SetBlipFlashes(blip, true)
  SetBlipAsShortRange(blip, false)
  BeginTextCommandSetBlipName('STRING')
  AddTextComponentSubstringPlayerName(Pure.shown('911 ' .. tostring(p.number or '')))
  EndTextCommandSetBlipName(blip)
  SetTimeout(Config.blips.seconds * 1000, function()
    if DoesBlipExist(blip) then RemoveBlip(blip) end
  end)
end

RegisterNetEvent('statewide:client:911', function(p)
  if type(p) ~= 'table' then return end
  Notify.show(L('push_911', Pure.push911Detail(p)), 'alert')
  if Config.blips.call911 and Pure.validCoords(p.coords) then callBlip(p) end
end)

RegisterNetEvent('statewide:client:311', function(p)
  if type(p) ~= 'table' then return end
  Notify.show(L('push_311', Pure.push911Detail(p)), 'info')
end)

RegisterNetEvent('statewide:client:panic', function(p)
  if type(p) ~= 'table' then return end
  if p.masked then return Notify.show(L('push_panic_masked', Pure.maskedPanicDetail(p, L('push_unit'))), 'alert') end
  Notify.show(L('push_panic', Pure.panicDetail(p)), 'alert')
end)

local units = {}
local unitState = {}

RegisterNetEvent('statewide:client:units', function(msg)
  local list = Pure.applyUnits(unitState, msg)
  if not list then return TriggerServerEvent('statewide:unitsSync') end
  units = list
  TriggerEvent('statewide:units', list)
end)

exports('getUnits', function()
  return units
end)

RegisterNetEvent('statewide:client:attached', function(p)
  if type(p) ~= 'table' then return end
  Notify.show(L('push_attached', Pure.attachedDetail(p)), 'info')
end)

RegisterNetEvent('statewide:client:waypoint', function(p)
  if type(p) ~= 'table' or not Pure.validWaypoint(p.x, p.y) then return end
  SetNewWaypoint(p.x + 0.0, p.y + 0.0)
  Notify.show(L('push_waypoint', type(p.label) == 'string' and p.label:sub(1, 40) or ''), 'info')
end)

RegisterNetEvent('statewide:client:callClosed', function(p)
  if type(p) ~= 'table' then return end
  local key, args = Pure.closedLine(p)
  Notify.show(L(key, table.unpack(args)), 'info')
end)

RegisterNetEvent('statewide:client:forcedOff', function(p)
  if type(p) ~= 'table' then return end
  Notify.show(L('push_forced_off', p.by or 'dispatch'), 'alert')
end)

RegisterNetEvent('statewide:client:vehicleInfo', function()
  local vehicle = GetVehiclePedIsIn(PlayerPedId(), false)
  if not vehicle or vehicle == 0 then return TriggerServerEvent('statewide:vehicle') end
  local model = GetEntityModel(vehicle)
  local make = GetMakeNameFromVehicleModel(model)
  local display = GetDisplayNameFromVehicleModel(model)
  TriggerServerEvent('statewide:vehicle', Pure.vehicleLabel(make, GetLabelText(make)), Pure.vehicleLabel(display, GetLabelText(display)), display)
end)

-- Cfx.re Lua runtime (client and server): state bags and the Entity/Player
-- wrappers, from `scheduler.lua`. The state bag natives (AddStateBagChangeHandler,
-- GetStateBagValue, ...) come from the generated native libraries. `LocalPlayer`
-- is client-only and declared in `client/client_statebags.lua`.

---
--- A state bag: a set of key/value pairs attached to the server (`GlobalState`),
--- an entity (`Entity(handle).state`) or a player (`Player(id).state`), and
--- synchronized between the server and the clients.
---
--- * Read a value with `bag.key` or `bag['key']` (`nil` when unset).
--- * Write with `bag.key = value`: replicated when written by the server,
---   local only when written by a client.
--- * Write with `bag:set(key, value, replicated)` to choose explicitly.
---
--- Values are serialized with msgpack. Writes are subject to the server
--- policy: the global bag is server-only, player bags can be written by their
--- player and the server, entity bags by the entity owner and the server.
---
--- [Documentation](https://docs.fivem.net/docs/scripting-manual/networking/state-bags/)
---@class StateBag
local StateBagType = {}

---
--- Sets `key` to `value`, choosing whether the change is replicated.
---
--- ```lua
--- Player(source).state:set('job', 'police', true)
--- ```
---@overload fun(key:string, value:any)
---@param key string @The key to set.
---@param value any @The new value; it must be serializable with msgpack.
---@param replicated boolean @`true` to replicate the change to the other side (default `false`).
function StateBagType:set(key, value, replicated) end

---
--- Wrapper returned by `Entity(handle)`, giving access to the entity state bag.
---@class CfxEntity
---@field state StateBag @The entity state bag (`entity:<netId>` for networked entities, `localEntity:<handle>` otherwise).
local CfxEntityType = {}

---
--- Wrapper returned by `Player(id)`, giving access to the player state bag.
---@class CfxPlayer
---@field state StateBag @The player state bag (`player:<serverId>`).
local CfxPlayerType = {}

---
--- Wraps an entity handle to access its state bag.
---
--- On the server, and for networked entities on the client, the bag is keyed
--- by the network id. Non-networked client entities get a local-only bag.
--- Assigning fields on the wrapper itself raises an error: write through
--- `state` instead.
---
--- ```lua
--- local vehicle = GetVehiclePedIsIn(PlayerPedId(), false)
--- print(Entity(vehicle).state.fuel)
--- ```
---
--- [Documentation](https://docs.fivem.net/docs/scripting-manual/networking/state-bags/)
---@param entity integer|CfxEntity @The entity handle. An existing wrapper is returned unchanged.
---@return CfxEntity @The entity wrapper.
function Entity(entity) end

---
--- Wraps a player to access its state bag.
---
--- `id` is the player server id (`source` on the server). On the client, `-1`
--- designates the local player (see `LocalPlayer`).
---
--- ```lua
--- Player(source).state.job = 'police'
--- ```
---
--- [Documentation](https://docs.fivem.net/docs/scripting-manual/networking/state-bags/)
---@param id integer|string|CfxPlayer @The player server id. An existing wrapper is returned unchanged.
---@return CfxPlayer @The player wrapper.
function Player(id) end

---
--- The global state bag, shared by the server and all clients. Only the server
--- can write to it.
---
--- ```lua
--- GlobalState.weather = 'RAIN'
--- ```
---
--- [Documentation](https://docs.fivem.net/docs/scripting-manual/networking/state-bags/)
---@type StateBag
GlobalState = nil

Notify = {}

local colors = { info = Config.chat.color, success = { 69, 165, 87 }, error = { 229, 72, 77 }, alert = { 247, 107, 21 } }

function Notify.show(text, kind)
  TriggerEvent('chat:addMessage', { color = colors[kind] or colors.info, args = { Config.chat.prefix, Pure.chatText(text) } })
  BeginTextCommandThefeedPost('STRING')
  AddTextComponentSubstringPlayerName(Pure.feedText(text))
  EndTextCommandThefeedPostTicker(kind == 'alert', true)
end

RegisterNetEvent('statewide:client:notify', function(text, kind)
  if type(text) ~= 'string' then return end
  Notify.show(text, kind)
end)

-- Cfx.re Lua runtime (client and server): CfxLua (LuaGLM) vector, quaternion
-- and matrix value types, their global constructors and the grit-compatible
-- helpers registered in the base library (lbaselib.c / lglm.cpp of
-- citizenfx/lua). The full `glm` library is only available through
-- `require 'glm'` and is not described here.

---
--- A 2-component vector. Vectors are immutable value types: `type(v)` is
--- `'vector2'` and assigning a component (`v.x = 1`) raises an error; build a
--- new vector instead (`v = v + vector2(1, 0)`).
---
--- * Components: `v.x`, `v.y`, the aliases `v.r`, `v.g`, or `v[1]`, `v[2]`.
--- * Swizzles: any sequence of 2 to 4 of the letters `x` and `y` (`v.yx`,
---   `v.xyxy`, ...) returns a vector of that size.
--- * `#v` is the magnitude (length) of the vector, not its component count.
--- * Arithmetic (`+ - * / // % ^`, unary `-`) works component-wise with other
---   vectors and with numbers. `==` compares components; `<` and `<=` raise
---   an error.
--- * `..` converts the vector to a string, like a number
---   (`'pos: ' .. v`).
---
--- [Documentation](https://docs.fivem.net/docs/scripting-reference/runtimes/lua/functions/vector2/)
---@class vector2
---@field x number @First component.
---@field y number @Second component.
---@field r number @Alias of `x`.
---@field g number @Alias of `y`.
---@field n integer @Number of components (2).
---@field dim integer @Number of components (2).
---@field xy vector2 @Swizzle: `vector2(v.x, v.y)`.
local Vector2Type = {}

---
--- A 3-component vector, used for world positions, rotations and directions.
--- Vectors are immutable value types: `type(v)` is `'vector3'` and assigning a
--- component (`v.x = 1`) raises an error; build a new vector instead
--- (`coords = coords + vector3(0.0, 0.0, 1.0)`).
---
--- * Components: `v.x`, `v.y`, `v.z`, the aliases `v.r`, `v.g`, `v.b`, or
---   `v[1]` to `v[3]`.
--- * Swizzles: any sequence of 2 to 4 of the letters `x`, `y` and `z`
---   (`v.xy`, `v.zyx`, ...) returns a vector of that size.
--- * `#v` is the magnitude (length) of the vector, so `#(a - b)` is the
---   distance between two points.
--- * Arithmetic (`+ - * / // % ^`, unary `-`) works component-wise with other
---   vectors and with numbers. `==` compares components; `<` and `<=` raise
---   an error.
--- * `..` converts the vector to a string, like a number.
--- * A `vector3` passed to a native is expanded into its `x, y, z` arguments
---   (except with `use_experimental_fxv2_oal` in the manifest).
---
--- [Documentation](https://docs.fivem.net/docs/scripting-reference/runtimes/lua/functions/vector3/)
---@class vector3
---@field x number @First component.
---@field y number @Second component.
---@field z number @Third component.
---@field r number @Alias of `x`.
---@field g number @Alias of `y`.
---@field b number @Alias of `z`.
---@field n integer @Number of components (3).
---@field dim integer @Number of components (3).
---@field xy vector2 @Swizzle: `vector2(v.x, v.y)`.
---@field xz vector2 @Swizzle: `vector2(v.x, v.z)`.
---@field yz vector2 @Swizzle: `vector2(v.y, v.z)`.
---@field xyz vector3 @Swizzle: `vector3(v.x, v.y, v.z)`.
local Vector3Type = {}

---
--- A 4-component vector, commonly used for a position plus a heading
--- (`w`). Vectors are immutable value types: `type(v)` is `'vector4'` and
--- assigning a component raises an error.
---
--- * Components: `v.x`, `v.y`, `v.z`, `v.w`, the aliases `v.r`, `v.g`, `v.b`,
---   `v.a`, or `v[1]` to `v[4]`.
--- * Swizzles: any sequence of 2 to 4 of the letters `x`, `y`, `z` and `w`
---   (`v.xyz`, `v.wzyx`, ...) returns a vector of that size.
--- * `#v` is the magnitude (length) of the vector.
--- * Arithmetic (`+ - * / // % ^`, unary `-`) works component-wise with other
---   vectors and with numbers. `==` compares components; `<` and `<=` raise
---   an error.
--- * `..` converts the vector to a string, like a number.
---
--- [Documentation](https://docs.fivem.net/docs/scripting-reference/runtimes/lua/functions/vector4/)
---@class vector4
---@field x number @First component.
---@field y number @Second component.
---@field z number @Third component.
---@field w number @Fourth component.
---@field r number @Alias of `x`.
---@field g number @Alias of `y`.
---@field b number @Alias of `z`.
---@field a number @Alias of `w`.
---@field n integer @Number of components (4).
---@field dim integer @Number of components (4).
---@field xy vector2 @Swizzle: `vector2(v.x, v.y)`.
---@field xz vector2 @Swizzle: `vector2(v.x, v.z)`.
---@field xw vector2 @Swizzle: `vector2(v.x, v.w)`.
---@field yz vector2 @Swizzle: `vector2(v.y, v.z)`.
---@field yw vector2 @Swizzle: `vector2(v.y, v.w)`.
---@field zw vector2 @Swizzle: `vector2(v.z, v.w)`.
---@field xyz vector3 @Swizzle: `vector3(v.x, v.y, v.z)`, for example the position part of a position + heading.
---@field xyw vector3 @Swizzle: `vector3(v.x, v.y, v.w)`.
---@field xzw vector3 @Swizzle: `vector3(v.x, v.z, v.w)`.
---@field yzw vector3 @Swizzle: `vector3(v.y, v.z, v.w)`.
---@field xyzw vector4 @Swizzle: `vector4(v.x, v.y, v.z, v.w)`.
local Vector4Type = {}

---
--- A quaternion (rotation). Quaternions are immutable value types:
--- `type(q)` is `'quat'`.
---
--- * Components: `q.x`, `q.y`, `q.z`, `q.w`, or `q[1]` to `q[4]`; swizzles
---   such as `q.xyz` (the vector part) work as on vectors.
--- * `q.angle` (degrees) and `q.axis` give the rotation as an angle and an
---   axis; they are not available after `require 'glm'`.
--- * `q * v` rotates the `vector3` `v`; `q1 * q2` composes rotations.
--- * `#q` is the magnitude of the quaternion (1 for a rotation).
---
--- [Documentation](https://docs.fivem.net/docs/scripting-reference/runtimes/lua/functions/quat/)
---@class quat
---@field x number @X component of the vector part.
---@field y number @Y component of the vector part.
---@field z number @Z component of the vector part.
---@field w number @Scalar part.
---@field n integer @Number of components (4).
---@field dim integer @Number of components (4).
---@field angle number @Rotation angle in degrees.
---@field axis vector3 @Rotation axis.
---@field xyz vector3 @Swizzle: the vector part, `vector3(q.x, q.y, q.z)`.
local QuatType = {}

---
--- A matrix of 2 to 4 columns and rows (`type(m)` is `'matrix'`). Unlike
--- vectors, matrices are mutable reference values. `m[i]` is the column `i` as
--- a vector (and can be assigned), `#m` is the number of columns, `m * v`
--- transforms a vector and `m1 * m2` multiplies matrices.
---@class matrix
local MatrixType = {}

---
--- Creates a `vector2`. A single number is copied to both components; a
--- larger vector is truncated to its first two components.
---
--- ```lua
--- local v = vector2(1.0, 2.0)
--- ```
---
--- [Documentation](https://docs.fivem.net/docs/scripting-reference/runtimes/lua/functions/vector2/)
---@overload fun(value:number):vector2
---@overload fun(v:vector2|vector3|vector4):vector2
---@param x number @First component.
---@param y number @Second component.
---@return vector2 @The new vector.
function vector2(x, y) end

---
--- Alias of `vector2`: creates a `vector2`.
---@overload fun(value:number):vector2
---@overload fun(v:vector2|vector3|vector4):vector2
---@param x number @First component.
---@param y number @Second component.
---@return vector2 @The new vector.
function vec2(x, y) end

---
--- Creates a `vector3` from 3 components. A single number is copied to every
--- component, vector arguments are expanded into their components, and a
--- single `vector4` is truncated to its first three components.
---
--- ```lua
--- local coords = vector3(-542.9, -208.3, 37.6)
--- local up = vector3(coords.xy, coords.z + 1.0)
--- ```
---
--- [Documentation](https://docs.fivem.net/docs/scripting-reference/runtimes/lua/functions/vector3/)
---@overload fun(value:number):vector3
---@overload fun(xy:vector2, z:number):vector3
---@overload fun(x:number, yz:vector2):vector3
---@overload fun(v:vector3|vector4):vector3
---@param x number @First component.
---@param y number @Second component.
---@param z number @Third component.
---@return vector3 @The new vector.
function vector3(x, y, z) end

---
--- Alias of `vector3`: creates a `vector3`.
---@overload fun(value:number):vector3
---@overload fun(xy:vector2, z:number):vector3
---@overload fun(x:number, yz:vector2):vector3
---@overload fun(v:vector3|vector4):vector3
---@param x number @First component.
---@param y number @Second component.
---@param z number @Third component.
---@return vector3 @The new vector.
function vec3(x, y, z) end

---
--- Creates a `vector4` from 4 components. A single number is copied to every
--- component and vector or quaternion arguments are expanded into their
--- components.
---
--- ```lua
--- local spawn = vector4(-542.9, -208.3, 37.6, 90.0)
--- local spawn2 = vector4(GetEntityCoords(PlayerPedId()), GetEntityHeading(PlayerPedId()))
--- ```
---
--- [Documentation](https://docs.fivem.net/docs/scripting-reference/runtimes/lua/functions/vector4/)
---@overload fun(value:number):vector4
---@overload fun(xyz:vector3, w:number):vector4
---@overload fun(xy:vector2, zw:vector2):vector4
---@overload fun(xy:vector2, z:number, w:number):vector4
---@overload fun(x:number, yzw:vector3):vector4
---@overload fun(x:number, yz:vector2, w:number):vector4
---@overload fun(x:number, y:number, zw:vector2):vector4
---@overload fun(v:vector4|quat):vector4
---@param x number @First component.
---@param y number @Second component.
---@param z number @Third component.
---@param w number @Fourth component.
---@return vector4 @The new vector.
function vector4(x, y, z, w) end

---
--- Alias of `vector4`: creates a `vector4`.
---@overload fun(value:number):vector4
---@overload fun(xyz:vector3, w:number):vector4
---@overload fun(xy:vector2, zw:vector2):vector4
---@overload fun(xy:vector2, z:number, w:number):vector4
---@overload fun(x:number, yzw:vector3):vector4
---@overload fun(x:number, yz:vector2, w:number):vector4
---@overload fun(x:number, y:number, zw:vector2):vector4
---@overload fun(v:vector4|quat):vector4
---@param x number @First component.
---@param y number @Second component.
---@param z number @Third component.
---@param w number @Fourth component.
---@return vector4 @The new vector.
function vec4(x, y, z, w) end

---
--- Creates a 1-component vector, which is a plain number.
---
--- [Documentation](https://docs.fivem.net/docs/scripting-reference/runtimes/lua/functions/vector1/)
---@param x number @The value.
---@return number @The value as a float.
function vector1(x) end

---
--- Alias of `vector1`: returns the value as a plain number.
---@param x number @The value.
---@return number @The value as a float.
function vec1(x) end

---
--- Creates a vector whose size is the total number of components given:
--- numbers count for one component, vectors and quaternions are expanded.
--- One component gives a number, 2 to 4 give a `vector2`, `vector3` or
--- `vector4`.
---
--- ```lua
--- local v = vector(1, 2, 3) -- vector3
--- ```
---
--- [Documentation](https://docs.fivem.net/docs/scripting-reference/runtimes/lua/functions/vector/)
---@vararg number|vector2|vector3|vector4|quat
---@return number|vector2|vector3|vector4 @The new vector.
function vector(...) end

---
--- Alias of `vector`: creates a vector sized by its number of components.
---@vararg number|vector2|vector3|vector4|quat
---@return number|vector2|vector3|vector4 @The new vector.
function vec(...) end

---
--- Like `vector`, but every component is truncated to an integer (the vector
--- still stores floats).
---@vararg number|vector2|vector3|vector4|quat
---@return number|vector2|vector3|vector4 @The new vector.
function ivec(...) end

---
--- Like `vector1`, but the value is truncated to an integer.
---@param x number @The value.
---@return number @The truncated value.
function ivec1(x) end

---
--- Like `vector2`, but every component is truncated to an integer.
---@overload fun(value:number):vector2
---@param x number @First component.
---@param y number @Second component.
---@return vector2 @The new vector.
function ivec2(x, y) end

---
--- Like `vector3`, but every component is truncated to an integer.
---@overload fun(value:number):vector3
---@param x number @First component.
---@param y number @Second component.
---@param z number @Third component.
---@return vector3 @The new vector.
function ivec3(x, y, z) end

---
--- Like `vector4`, but every component is truncated to an integer.
---@overload fun(value:number):vector4
---@param x number @First component.
---@param y number @Second component.
---@param z number @Third component.
---@param w number @Fourth component.
---@return vector4 @The new vector.
function ivec4(x, y, z, w) end

---
--- Like `vector`, but every component is converted to a boolean (stored as
--- `1` or `0`).
---@vararg any
---@return number|vector2|vector3|vector4 @The new vector.
function bvec(...) end

---
--- Like `vector1`, but the value is converted to a boolean (`1` or `0`).
---@param x any @The value.
---@return number @`1` or `0`.
function bvec1(x) end

---
--- Like `vector2`, but every component is converted to a boolean (`1` or `0`).
---@overload fun(value:any):vector2
---@param x any @First component.
---@param y any @Second component.
---@return vector2 @The new vector.
function bvec2(x, y) end

---
--- Like `vector3`, but every component is converted to a boolean (`1` or `0`).
---@overload fun(value:any):vector3
---@param x any @First component.
---@param y any @Second component.
---@param z any @Third component.
---@return vector3 @The new vector.
function bvec3(x, y, z) end

---
--- Like `vector4`, but every component is converted to a boolean (`1` or `0`).
---@overload fun(value:any):vector4
---@param x any @First component.
---@param y any @Second component.
---@param z any @Third component.
---@param w any @Fourth component.
---@return vector4 @The new vector.
function bvec4(x, y, z, w) end

---
--- Creates a quaternion.
---
--- * `quat()`: the identity rotation.
--- * `quat(w, x, y, z)`: from components (note that `w` comes first).
--- * `quat(xyz, w)`: from the vector part and the scalar part.
--- * `quat(angle, axis)`: rotation of `angle` degrees around `axis`.
--- * `quat(from, to)`: shortest rotation from direction `from` to `to`.
--- * `quat(q)`: a copy of `q`.
--- * `quat(m)`: from a 3x3 or 4x4 rotation matrix.
---
--- ```lua
--- local rotation = quat(90.0, vector3(0.0, 0.0, 1.0))
--- local rotated = rotation * vector3(1.0, 0.0, 0.0)
--- ```
---
--- [Documentation](https://docs.fivem.net/docs/scripting-reference/runtimes/lua/functions/quat/)
---@overload fun():quat
---@overload fun(xyz:vector3, w:number):quat
---@overload fun(angle:number, axis:vector3):quat
---@overload fun(from:vector3, to:vector3):quat
---@overload fun(q:quat):quat
---@overload fun(m:matrix):quat
---@param w number @Scalar part.
---@param x number @X component of the vector part.
---@param y number @Y component of the vector part.
---@param z number @Z component of the vector part.
---@return quat @The new quaternion.
function quat(w, x, y, z) end

---
--- Alias of `quat`: creates a quaternion.
---@overload fun():quat
---@overload fun(xyz:vector3, w:number):quat
---@overload fun(angle:number, axis:vector3):quat
---@overload fun(from:vector3, to:vector3):quat
---@overload fun(q:quat):quat
---@overload fun(m:matrix):quat
---@param w number @Scalar part.
---@param x number @X component of the vector part.
---@param y number @Y component of the vector part.
---@param z number @Z component of the vector part.
---@return quat @The new quaternion.
function qua(w, x, y, z) end

---
--- Creates a matrix. A single number fills the diagonal, a quaternion gives
--- its rotation matrix, a matrix is resized, and otherwise each argument is a
--- column vector (the size is inferred from the arguments).
---@vararg number|vector2|vector3|vector4|quat|matrix
---@return matrix @The new matrix.
function mat(...) end

---
--- Creates a 2x2 matrix (see `mat` for the accepted arguments).
---@vararg number|vector2|quat|matrix
---@return matrix @The new matrix.
function mat2x2(...) end

---
--- Alias of `mat2x2`: creates a 2x2 matrix.
---@vararg number|vector2|quat|matrix
---@return matrix @The new matrix.
function mat2(...) end

---
--- Creates a matrix of 2 columns and 3 rows (see `mat`).
---@vararg number|vector3|quat|matrix
---@return matrix @The new matrix.
function mat2x3(...) end

---
--- Creates a matrix of 2 columns and 4 rows (see `mat`).
---@vararg number|vector4|quat|matrix
---@return matrix @The new matrix.
function mat2x4(...) end

---
--- Creates a matrix of 3 columns and 2 rows (see `mat`).
---@vararg number|vector2|quat|matrix
---@return matrix @The new matrix.
function mat3x2(...) end

---
--- Creates a 3x3 matrix (see `mat` for the accepted arguments).
---@vararg number|vector3|quat|matrix
---@return matrix @The new matrix.
function mat3x3(...) end

---
--- Alias of `mat3x3`: creates a 3x3 matrix.
---@vararg number|vector3|quat|matrix
---@return matrix @The new matrix.
function mat3(...) end

---
--- Creates a matrix of 3 columns and 4 rows (see `mat`).
---@vararg number|vector4|quat|matrix
---@return matrix @The new matrix.
function mat3x4(...) end

---
--- Creates a matrix of 4 columns and 2 rows (see `mat`).
---@vararg number|vector2|quat|matrix
---@return matrix @The new matrix.
function mat4x2(...) end

---
--- Creates a matrix of 4 columns and 3 rows (see `mat`).
---@vararg number|vector3|quat|matrix
---@return matrix @The new matrix.
function mat4x3(...) end

---
--- Creates a 4x4 matrix (see `mat` for the accepted arguments).
---@vararg number|vector4|quat|matrix
---@return matrix @The new matrix.
function mat4x4(...) end

---
--- Alias of `mat4x4`: creates a 4x4 matrix.
---@vararg number|vector4|quat|matrix
---@return matrix @The new matrix.
function mat4(...) end

---
--- Returns the dot product of two numbers, vectors of the same size or
--- quaternions.
---
--- [Documentation](https://docs.fivem.net/docs/scripting-reference/runtimes/lua/functions/dot/)
---@param a number|vector2|vector3|vector4|quat @First operand.
---@param b number|vector2|vector3|vector4|quat @Second operand, of the same type.
---@return number @The dot product.
function dot(a, b) end

---
--- Returns the cross product: a number for two `vector2`, a `vector3` for two
--- `vector3` (or a `vector3` and a `quat`), a `quat` for two quaternions.
---
--- [Documentation](https://docs.fivem.net/docs/scripting-reference/runtimes/lua/functions/cross/)
---@param a vector2|vector3|quat @First operand.
---@param b vector2|vector3|quat @Second operand.
---@return number|vector3|quat @The cross product.
function cross(a, b) end

---
--- Returns the inverse of a quaternion or of a square matrix.
---
--- [Documentation](https://docs.fivem.net/docs/scripting-reference/runtimes/lua/functions/inv/)
---@generic T
---@param value T @A `quat` or a square `matrix`.
---@return T @The inverse.
function inv(value) end

---
--- Returns the normalized vector or quaternion (same direction, length 1).
---
--- [Documentation](https://docs.fivem.net/docs/scripting-reference/runtimes/lua/functions/norm/)
---@generic T
---@param value T @A vector or a `quat`.
---@return T @The normalized value.
function norm(value) end

---
--- Spherical linear interpolation between two vectors of the same size, or
--- two quaternions, by the factor `t` (0 to 1).
---
--- [Documentation](https://docs.fivem.net/docs/scripting-reference/runtimes/lua/functions/slerp/)
---@generic T
---@param a T @The start value (a vector or a `quat`).
---@param b T @The end value, of the same type.
---@param t number @The interpolation factor.
---@return T @The interpolated value.
function slerp(a, b, t) end

-- Built-in Types

---
--- The type *nil* has one single value, **nil**, whose main property is to be 
--- different from any other value; it usually represents the absence of a 
--- useful value.
---@class nil

---
--- The type *boolean* has two values, **false** and **true**. Both **nil** and 
--- **false** make a condition false; any other value makes it true.
---@class boolean

---
--- The type *number* uses two internal representations, or two subtypes, one
--- called *integer* and the other called *float*. Lua has explicit rules about
--- when each representation is used, but it also converts between them
--- automatically as needed. Therefore, the programmer may choose to mostly
--- ignore the difference between integers and floats or to assume complete
--- control over the representation of each number. Standard Lua uses 64-bit
--- integers and double-precision (64-bit) floats, but you can also compile
--- Lua so that it uses 32-bit integers and/or single-precision (32-bit)
--- floats. The option with 32 bits for both integers and floats is
--- particularly attractive for small machines and embedded systems. (See
--- macro LUA_32BITS in file luaconf.h.)
---@class number

---
--- Lua can call (and manipulate) functions written in Lua and functions
--- written in C. Both are represented by the type *function*.
---@class function

---
--- The type *userdata* is provided to allow arbitrary C data to be stored in 
--- Lua variables. A userdata value represents a block of raw memory. There 
--- are two kinds of userdata: *full userdata*, which is an object with a block
--- of memory managed by Lua, and *light userdata*, which is simply a C pointer
--- value. Userdata has no predefined operations in Lua, except assignment 
--- and identity test. By using *metatables*, the programmer can define 
--- operations for full userdata values. Userdata values cannot be
--- created or modified in Lua, only through the C API. This guarantees the 
--- integrity of data owned by the host program.
---@class userdata

---
--- The type *thread* represents independent threads of execution and it is 
--- used to implement coroutines. Lua threads are not related to 
--- operating-system threads. Lua supports coroutines on all systems, even those
--- that do not support threads natively.
---@class thread

---
--- The type *table* implements associative arrays, that is, arrays that can
--- have as indices not only numbers, but any Lua value except **nil** and NaN.
--- (*Not a Number* is a special floating-point value used by the IEEE 754
--- standard to represent undefined or unrepresentable numerical results, such
--- as `0/0`.) Tables can be heterogeneous; that is, they can contain values of
--- all types (except **nil**). Any key with value **nil** is not considered
--- part oft he table. Conversely, any key that is not part of a table has an
--- a ssociated value **nil**.
---
--- Tables are the sole data-structuring mechanism in Lua; they can be used to
--- represent ordinary arrays, lists, symbol tables, sets, records, graphs,
--- trees, etc. To represent records, Lua uses the field name as an index. The
--- language supports this representation by providing `a.name` as syntactic
--- sugar for `a["name"]`. There are several convenient ways to create tables
--- in Lua.
---
--- Like indices, the values of table fields can be of any type. In particular,
--- because functions are first-class values, table fields can contain functions.
--- Thus tables can also carry *methods*.
---
--- The indexing of tables follows the definition of raw equality in the 
--- language. The expressions `a[i]` and `a[j]` denote the same table element
--- if and only if `i` and `j` are raw equal (that is, equal without 
--- metamethods). In particular, floats with integral values are equal to 
--- their respective integers. To avoid ambiguities, any float with integral 
--- value used as a key is converted to its respective integer. For instance,
--- if you write `a[2.0] = true`, the actual key inserted into the table will
--- be the integer `2`. (On the other hand, 2 and "`2`" are different Lua 
--- values and therefore denote different table entries.)
---@class table

---
--- Any of the above Built-in Types.
---@class any

---
---@class void

---@class self

local BAG = 'statewide:unregistered'

local function skipped(vehicle)
  local class = GetVehicleClass(vehicle)
  for _, c in ipairs(Config.registration.skipClasses or {}) do
    if c == class then return true end
  end
  return false
end

CreateThread(function()
  local last = 0
  while Pure.regMode(Config.registration) ~= 'off' do
    Wait(1000)
    local ped = PlayerPedId()
    local vehicle = GetVehiclePedIsIn(ped, false)
    if vehicle == 0 then
      last = 0
    elseif vehicle ~= last and GetPedInVehicleSeat(vehicle, -1) == ped then
      last = vehicle
      if LocalPlayer.state['statewide:unit'] == nil and not skipped(vehicle) then TriggerServerEvent('statewide:seat') end
    end
  end
end)

local holding = {}

AddStateBagChangeHandler(BAG, nil, function(bagName, _, value)
  if value ~= true then return end
  local vehicle = GetEntityFromStateBagName(bagName)
  if not vehicle or vehicle == 0 or holding[vehicle] then return end
  holding[vehicle] = true
  CreateThread(function()
    while DoesEntityExist(vehicle) and Entity(vehicle).state[BAG] == true do
      if GetPedInVehicleSeat(vehicle, -1) == PlayerPedId() and GetIsVehicleEngineRunning(vehicle) then SetVehicleEngineOn(vehicle, false, true, true) end
      Wait(500)
    end
    holding[vehicle] = nil
  end)
end)

local busy = false
local promptOpen = false

local function showPrompt()
    if promptOpen then return end
    lib.showTextUI(locale('wash_prompt', Config.Price), { icon = 'spray-can-sparkles' })
    promptOpen = true
end

local function hidePrompt()
    if not promptOpen then return end
    lib.hideTextUI()
    promptOpen = false
end

local function startWash(station, vehicle)
    busy = true
    hidePrompt()

    local paid = lib.callback.await('douro_carwash:pay', false, station)
    if not paid then
        busy = false
        return
    end

    FreezeEntityPosition(vehicle, true)

    local finished = lib.progressCircle({
        duration = Config.Duration,
        label = locale('washing'),
        position = 'bottom',
        canCancel = false,
        disable = { move = true, car = true, combat = true },
    })

    if finished and DoesEntityExist(vehicle) then
        SetVehicleDirtLevel(vehicle, 0.0)
        WashDecalsFromVehicle(vehicle, 1.0)
        lib.notify({ type = 'success', description = locale('done') })
    end

    FreezeEntityPosition(vehicle, false)
    busy = false
end

for index, coords in ipairs(Config.Stations) do
    if Config.Blip then
        local blip = AddBlipForCoord(coords.x, coords.y, coords.z)
        SetBlipSprite(blip, Config.Blip.sprite)
        SetBlipColour(blip, Config.Blip.color)
        SetBlipScale(blip, Config.Blip.scale)
        SetBlipAsShortRange(blip, true)
        BeginTextCommandSetBlipName('STRING')
        AddTextComponentSubstringPlayerName(locale('blip'))
        EndTextCommandSetBlipName(blip)
    end

    -- lib.points only runs nearby() while the player is inside the radius,
    -- so the resource stays at 0.00 ms everywhere else.
    local point = lib.points.new({
        coords = coords,
        distance = Config.Radius,
        station = index,
    })

    function point:onExit()
        hidePrompt()
    end

    function point:nearby()
        if busy then return end

        local vehicle = cache.vehicle
        if not vehicle or cache.seat ~= -1 then
            hidePrompt()
            return
        end

        showPrompt()

        if IsControlJustReleased(0, 38) then -- E
            startWash(self.station, vehicle)
        end
    end
end

AddEventHandler('onResourceStop', function(resource)
    if resource == GetCurrentResourceName() then
        hidePrompt()
    end
end)

coroutine = {}

---
--- Creates a new coroutine, with body `f`. `f` must be a Lua function. Returns
--- this new coroutine, an object with type `"thread"`.
---@param f fun():thread
---@return thread
function coroutine.create(f) end

---
--- Returns true when the running coroutine can yield.
---
--- A running coroutine is yieldable if it is not the main thread and it is not
--- inside a non-yieldable C function.
---@return boolean
function coroutine.isyieldable() end

---
--- Starts or continues the execution of coroutine `co`. The first time you
--- resume a coroutine, it starts running its body. The values `val1`, ...
--- are passed as the arguments to the body function. If the coroutine has
--- yielded, `resume` restarts it; the values `val1`, ... are passed as the
--- results from the yield.
---
--- If the coroutine runs without any errors, `resume` returns **true** plus any
--- values passed to `yield` (when the coroutine yields) or any values returned
--- by the body function (when the coroutine terminates). If there is any error,
--- `resume` returns **false** plus the error message.
---@overload fun(co:thread):boolean|any
---@param co thread
---@param val1 string
---@return thread|any
function coroutine.resume(co, val1, ...) end

---
--- Returns the running coroutine plus a boolean, true when the running
--- coroutine is the main one.
---@return thread|boolean
function coroutine.running() end

---
--- Returns the status of coroutine `co`, as a string: "`running`", if the
--- coroutine is running (that is, it called `status`); "`suspended`", if the
--- coroutine is suspended in a call to `yield`, or if it has not started
--- running yet; "`normal`" if the coroutine is active but not running (that
--- is, it has resumed another coroutine); and "`dead`" if the coroutine has
--- finished its body function, or if it has stopped with an error.
---@param co thread
---@return string
function coroutine.status(co) end

---
--- Creates a new coroutine, with body `f`. `f` must be a Lua function. Returns
--- a function that resumes the coroutine each time it is called. Any arguments
--- passed to the function behave as the extra arguments to `resume`. Returns
--- the same values returned by `resume`, except the first
--- boolean. In case of error, propagates the error.
---@param f fun():thread
---@return fun():any
function coroutine.wrap(f) end

---
--- Suspends the execution of the calling coroutine. Any arguments to `yield`
--- are passed as extra results to `resume`.
---@return any
function coroutine.yield(...) end

local blips = {}
local keys = {}

local function addBlip(m)
  local kind = Pure.SCENE_MARKER_KINDS[m.kind]
  local blip = AddBlipForCoord(m.x, m.y, 0.0)
  SetBlipSprite(blip, kind.sprite)
  SetBlipColour(blip, kind.colour)
  SetBlipScale(blip, 0.9)
  SetBlipAsShortRange(blip, false)
  BeginTextCommandSetBlipName('STRING')
  AddTextComponentSubstringPlayerName(Pure.sceneBlipName(m))
  EndTextCommandSetBlipName(blip)
  return blip
end

local function dropBlip(id)
  local blip = blips[id]
  if blip and DoesBlipExist(blip) then RemoveBlip(blip) end
  blips[id] = nil
  keys[id] = nil
end

RegisterNetEvent('statewide:client:sceneMarkers', function(list)
  if type(list) ~= 'table' then return end
  local add, remove = Pure.sceneBlipChanges(keys, list)
  for _, id in ipairs(remove) do dropBlip(id) end
  for _, m in ipairs(add) do
    blips[m.id] = addBlip(m)
    keys[m.id] = Pure.sceneBlipKey(m)
  end
end)

AddEventHandler('onResourceStop', function(name)
  if name ~= GetCurrentResourceName() then return end
  for id in pairs(blips) do dropBlip(id) end
end)

local KVP = 'statewide:tablet:rect'
local KVP_SCALE = 'statewide:tablet:scale'
local isOpen, waiting, shown, escaping = false, false, false, false

local function savedRect()
  local raw = GetResourceKvpString(KVP)
  if not raw or raw == '' then return nil end
  local ok, r = pcall(json.decode, raw)
  if ok and Pure.validRect(r) then return r end
  return nil
end

local function savedScale()
  local s = GetResourceKvpFloat(KVP_SCALE)
  if Pure.validScale(s) then return s end
  return nil
end

local function close()
  isOpen, waiting = false, false
  SetNuiFocus(false, false)
  SendNUIMessage({ type = 'close' })
end

local function vehicleOk()
  if not Config.tablet.vehicleOnly then return true end
  local vehicle = GetVehiclePedIsIn(PlayerPedId(), false)
  if vehicle == 0 then return false end
  return Pure.tabletVehicleAllowed(Config.tablet, GetVehicleClass(vehicle), GetEntityModel(vehicle), GetHashKey)
end

local function watchVehicle()
  CreateThread(function()
    while isOpen do
      Wait(500)
      if isOpen and not vehicleOk() then close() end
    end
  end)
end

local function watchEscape()
  if escaping then return end
  escaping = true
  CreateThread(function()
    while isOpen and not shown do
      DisableControlAction(0, 200, true)
      if IsDisabledControlJustReleased(0, 200) then close() end
      Wait(0)
    end
    escaping = false
  end)
end

local function open()
  if isOpen then return close() end
  if not vehicleOk() then return Notify.show(L('tablet_vehicle_only'), 'error') end
  isOpen, waiting, shown = true, false, false
  SetNuiFocus(true, true)
  SendNUIMessage({
    type = 'open',
    rect = savedRect(),
    scale = Config.tablet.scale,
    savedScale = savedScale(),
    key = Config.tablet.key,
    keepMinutes = Config.tablet.keepMinutes,
    labels = {
      title = L('tablet_title'),
      reset = L('tablet_reset'),
      close = L('tablet_close'),
      smaller = L('tablet_smaller'),
      larger = L('tablet_larger'),
      loading = L('tablet_loading'),
      timeoutTitle = L('tablet_err_frame_timeout'),
      timeoutNext = L('tablet_next_frame_timeout'),
    },
  })
  watchEscape()
  if Config.tablet.vehicleOnly then watchVehicle() end
end

local function errorNext(code)
  if code == 'not_on_duty' then return L('tablet_next_not_on_duty', Config.commands.duty.name) end
  return Locale['tablet_next_' .. code] or L('tablet_next_generic')
end

RegisterNetEvent('statewide:client:tablet', function(p)
  if type(p) ~= 'table' then return end
  if p.drop == true then return SendNUIMessage({ type = 'drop' }) end
  if not isOpen or not waiting then return end
  waiting = false
  local payload = Pure.tabletPayload({ url = p.url, tabletToken = p.token, linkCode = p.link })
  if payload then return SendNUIMessage({ type = 'url', url = payload.url, token = payload.token, link = payload.link }) end
  local code = type(p.error) == 'string' and p.error:match('^[%w_]+$') and p.error or 'error'
  SendNUIMessage({
    type = 'error',
    code = code,
    title = Locale['tablet_err_' .. code] or L('tablet_err_generic'),
    next = errorNext(code),
  })
end)

RegisterNUICallback('code', function(_, cb)
  cb({})
  if not isOpen then return end
  waiting, shown = true, false
  watchEscape()
  TriggerServerEvent('statewide:tablet')
end)

RegisterNUICallback('close', function(_, cb)
  close()
  cb({})
end)

RegisterNUICallback('shown', function(_, cb)
  shown = true
  cb({})
end)

RegisterNUICallback('rect', function(data, cb)
  if type(data) == 'table' and data.reset == true then
    DeleteResourceKvp(KVP)
    DeleteResourceKvp(KVP_SCALE)
  elseif Pure.validRect(data) then
    SetResourceKvp(KVP, json.encode({ x = math.floor(data.x), y = math.floor(data.y), w = math.floor(data.w), h = math.floor(data.h) }))
  end
  cb({})
end)

RegisterNUICallback('scale', function(data, cb)
  if type(data) == 'table' and Pure.validScale(data.scale) then SetResourceKvpFloat(KVP_SCALE, data.scale) end
  cb({})
end)

AddEventHandler('onResourceStop', function(name)
  if name == GetCurrentResourceName() then SetNuiFocus(false, false) end
end)

if Config.tablet.enabled then
  RegisterCommand(Config.tablet.command, open, false)
  RegisterKeyMapping(Config.tablet.command, L('cmd_tablet'), 'keyboard', Config.tablet.key)
  CreateThread(function()
    Wait(1000)
    TriggerEvent('chat:addSuggestion', '/' .. Config.tablet.command, L('cmd_tablet'), {})
  end)
end

---
--- Enters an interactive mode with the user, running each string that the user
--- enters. Using simple commands and other debug facilities, the user can
--- inspect global and local variables, change their values, evaluate
--- expressions, and so on. A line containing only the word `cont` finishes this
--- function, so that the caller continues its execution.
---
--- Note that commands for `debug.debug` are not lexically nested within any
--- function, and so have no direct access to local variables.
function debug.debug() end

---
--- Returns the current hook settings of the thread, as three values: the
--- current hook function, the current hook mask, and the current hook count
--- (as set by the `debug.sethook` function).
---@overload fun():thread
---@param thread thread
---@return thread
function debug.gethook(thread) end

---@class DebugInfo
---@field linedefined number
---@field lastlinedefined number
---@field currentline number
---@field func function
---@field isvararg boolean
---@field namewhat string
---@field source string
---@field nups number
---@field what string
---@field nparams number
---@field short_src string

---
--- Returns a table with information about a function. You can give the
--- function directly, or you can give a number as the value of `f`,
--- which means the function running at level `f` of the call stack
--- of the given thread: level 0 is the current function (`getinfo` itself);
--- level 1 is the function that called `getinfo` (except for tail calls, which

---@param level number
